The owner of a one-room flat, where a 16-year-old Class 12 student was held captive for 24 hours and subjected to brutal sexual assault by a Thane youth, is set to face an FIR for not verifying his tenant, who posed as a NEET aspirant while seeking the rented room, said police. Article Title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
Article Text:
The Bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer” on the Indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country

NEW DELHI: With former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina ’s news conference kicking up a diplomatic firestorm, the government said on Friday her remarks, especially those related to the government in Dhaka, are not endorsed by India.“Government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity, and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted govt of Bangladesh,” said ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.Following this, Bangladesh had expressed outrage over the former PM’s remarks, saying the event had hurt the sentiments of its people and could adversely affect efforts to improve bilateral ties with India.The Bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer” on the Indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country and that Bangladesh would never be a client state.
Article Summary: Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina ’s news conference kicked up a diplomatic firestorm. The government said on Friday her remarks, especially those related to the government in Dhaka, are not endorsed by India. The Bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer” on the Indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country.

Article Title: Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhand’s largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: Protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday. Students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified. 11-member delegation finalised for talks with the state government.

Article Title: FCRA Bill 'internal matter': India rejects US criticism
Article Text:
Home minister Amit Shah has held meetings with representatives of church bodies to allay their concerns about the provisions of the bill

Government may push for FCRA Bill ’s passage before Friday

NEW DELHI: Amid indications it may seek the passage of the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Act, the government on Friday rejected criticism of the legislation by foreigners, including a US Congressman.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said several countries, including the US, regulate foreign funds and foreign financing. "As far as legislative matters are concerned, and particularly matters relating to India's own legislation, this is an internal matter for us, on which our Parliament takes the decision," Jaiswal said.The remarks came days after US Congressman Riley Moore criticised the move to tighten the FCRA law meant to regulate foreign contributions.According to reports, the Republican representative from West Virginia said the proposed amendments in the law would result in the takeover of churches and religious charities, and warned that the Bill’s passage would hurt the US’ ties with India. There are indications that the government may try to get the Bill passed next week despite the opposition’s decision to oppose it.Over the past couple of days, home minister Amit Shah has held meetings with representatives of church bodies to allay their concerns about the provisions of the Bill.Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma, who met Shah with representatives of church bodies, had said the Bill may be put up for consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Although the government is tightlipped about its plans, sources say there was a strong possibility of it pushing the contentious legislation before Friday when the monsoon Session is scheduled to conclude.Congress is said to have told the allies that the BJP may try to surprise the opposition by bringing the FCRA Bill on Monday, which is to be piloted by Shah, and all the parties should ensure attendance of their MPs. The allies may also issue a whip for the last week of the monsoon session.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said several countries, including the US, regulate foreign funds and foreign financing. US Congressman Riley Moore criticised the move to tighten the FCRA law. There are indications that the government may try to get the Bill passed next week despite the opposition’s decision to oppose it.

Article Title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement
Article Text:
MEA has dismissed as “fake news” a report claiming India sought a defence pact with Israel after the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security agreement.

With inputs from ANI

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact following the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The ministry called the claim “fake news” generated using artificial intelligence.The report, published by Turkish outlet Straturka and subsequently circulated on social media, claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security arrangement. The report cited unnamed Pakistani sources.The MEA’s Fact Check unit shared a screenshot of the report on X and flagged it as fake, warning users against what it described as malicious social media posts created using AI.“We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!” the ministry’s Fact Check wing said.The claim surfaced after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to deepen military and security cooperation among the three countries. Pakistan has described the agreement as a collective-deterrence arrangement, with its foreign ministry saying an armed attack on any one of the three signatories would be treated as an attack on all three.The agreement has drawn attention in New Delhi, with the MEA saying India is closely monitoring developments.“We are also closely following this development, and we shall keep you updated,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the ministry’s weekly briefing.The MEA’s clarification came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewed cooperation between the two countries across several areas.The conversation focused on strengthening bilateral ties and the existing partnership between India and Israel, rather than any new defence pact linked to the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey agreement.
Article Summary: The Ministry of External Affairs rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact. The claim surfaced after the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The report claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging security arrangement.

Article Title: BJP picks audio clip to target Cong over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
Article Text:
BJP demanded replies from Congress’ Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi on Congress functionaries' claim about money was exchanged for ministerial berths

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday seized on a leaked conversation allegedly between two Congress functionaries to claim that money was exchanged for ministerial berths in the recent expansion of the Karnataka cabinet and demanded replies from Congress’ Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.BJP MP Anurag Thakur’s attack on Congress came after Karnataka BJP’s Chalavadi Narayanaswamy cited the audio record to allege that cabinet positions in the state had been secured through monetary influence. According to the audio tape of the conversation, 80% of the ministers secured their posts in the state cabinet by making such offerings, he added.“In Congress, one’s stature and chair depend on the offering they make to its high command,” he said and cited the audio to wonder if a senior Congress functionary like HK Patil was denied a berth because he did not pay the bribe.“The question is why a person, who is an accused in the Valmiki Tribes Development Corporation scam and is still facing an ED case, has been inducted into the cabinet?” Thakur asked, in an apparent reference to B Nagendra.
Article Summary: BJP MP Anurag Thakur’s attack on Congress came after Karnataka BJP alleged that cabinet positions had been secured through monetary influence. According to the audio tape of the conversation, 80% of the ministers secured their posts in the state cabinet by making such offerings, he added.

Article Title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
Article Text:
With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved; Samrat Choudhary's council, constituted on May 7, included Prakash

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday sought records from the Bihar government relating to the appointment of Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year, his re-induction into the cabinet in May and his recent hurried nomination as an MLC allegedly to skirt around the six-month deadline within which such a minister must get elected to the House.A PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline within which a person, who is not a member of the assembly or legislative council, must get elected as a member of either house.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, for the Bihar government, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi, and V Mohana that the minister has since been nominated as an MLC by the governor; hence, his continuance was not unconstitutional.However, the petitioner, relying on the SC's 2001 judgment in the SR Chaudhari case, which had categorically stated that the six-month deadline was non-negotiable, said the six-month deadline expired on May 20. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. The new council of ministers was constituted under Samrat Choudhary on May 7, which included Prakash. The bench asked the Bihar government to place on record all documents relating to the appointment of Prakash in the first instance, his re-induction and subsequent nomination as MLC.In its 2001 judgment by a three-judge bench, SC had ruled, "Permitting a non-legislator minister to be re-appointed, without getting elected within the period prescribed by Article 164(4) (six months), would amount to ignoring the electorate in having its say as to who should represent it - a position which is wholly unacceptable."The seductive temptations to cling to office regardless of constitutional restraint must be totally eschewed. Will of the people cannot be permitted to be subordinated to political expediency of the prime minister or the chief minister as the case may be, to have in his cabinet a non-legislator as a minister for an indefinite period by repeated re-appointments without the individual seeking popular mandate of the electorate. "The SC added, "Chief ministers or governors must... not sacrifice either political responsibility or parliamentary conventions at the altar of political expediency."
Article Summary: Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year. PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. Samrat Choudhary's council, constituted on May 7, included P Rakash.

Article Title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
Article Text:
Kharge demands Amit Shah's statement in Rajya Sabha; Rijiju says "opposition will not decide which minister comes to House"

NEW DELHI: Amid continuing opposition protests lampooning home minister Amit Shah for his "absence" from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju Friday said the opposition cannot decide which minister will come to the House and speak.With the Lok Sabha paralysed and a virtual washout of Parliament's monsoon session looming, Rijiju said Shah comes to Parliament building every day and stays till late at night. "Shah is a man whose name sends shivers down the spine of extremists and terrorists," he said, amid the thumping of desks by members of the treasury benches. "The day the discussion begins here, and when Amit Shah responds, you (opposition) won't be able to sit through it," he said.Protests by opposition MPs forced the chairs of both Houses to adjourn the proceedings till Monday. The opposition has put Shah at the centre of its protests against alleged police excesses against protesters organised under the banner of Cockroach Janta Party who defied prohibitory orders to march towards Parliament. The Lok Sabha could not function as opposition MPs held placards and raised slogans demanding that Shah come to the House and respond to the police action on student protesters.They also held placards designed as attendance sheets, with 'nil' against Shah. The House passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid the din, without debate.The confrontation looks set to be extended to any discussion on the FCRA Bill in case the government seeks to push the legislation that has been opposed by opposition parties and church and Muslim bodies. Shah is likely to participate in the debate.

Article Title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
Article Text:
With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Mahua Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition. (File photo)

NEW DELHI: "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest?" the Supreme Court remarked on Friday while refusing to entertain Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra 's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in connection with a hate speech case.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law."The requirement as per the police's notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency. Last time I went there two things happened. First there were threats that eggs will be thrown etc. and second time eggs were actually thrown," he submitted.The bench, however, was unconvinced and orally observed, "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs?"When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all," it added, according to news agency PTI.With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition, following which it was dismissed as withdrawn.The plea challenged a July 21 order of the Calcutta High Court, which had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action until October 5 in the hate speech case, while directing her to cooperate with the investigation.The MP has claimed the case registered at Hogolberia Police Station in Nadia district is based on fabricated allegations. She had sought the quashing of the proceedings and protection from any coercive action by the police.Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya of the Calcutta high court had directed Moitra to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning and ordered that no coercive steps be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the investigation.The high court had noted that the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita invoked against Moitra carry a maximum punishment of less than seven years, making her eligible for protection from coercive action as long as she cooperates with the probe.The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the high court again on October 1.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to entertain Mahua Moitra's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.

Article Title: PM Modi's meet with Badal fuels buzz about BJP-SAD pact
Article Text:
SAD leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with BJP, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since AAP came to office in 2022

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, fuelling buzz about the revival of the alliance between their parties in the sharply fragmented political space of Punjab as the state gears up for assembly elections next year.While the BJP brass has publicly maintained it will go solo, a prospect that has acquired seriousness as the party has expanded on the back of regional satraps joining it from different parties, a section of its state leadership has batted for renewing ties with the estranged ally due to its perceived political and social dividends.That PM Modi met Sukhbir suggests a rethink. SAD leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with BJP, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since AAP came to office in 2022. It has shrunk to three MLAs and an MP.What has likely raised the possibility of their alliance is the growing realisation that a division of votes among four parties, factionalism-hit Congress being the other party in reckoning, may help AAP despite the perceived anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led government. Badal is believed to have raised the issue of "crumbling" law and order and "rampant" corruption in Punjab under the AAP government in his meeting with PM Modi.Besides, the entry of jailed MP Amritpal Singh-led Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), which appeals to a radical section with pro-Khalistan impulses, has given Punjab politics another dimension in the run up to the polls and might have prompted the BJP to look afresh at its future course of action in the state. Even though the politics of their alliance makes much sense, what has been a sticking point is the likely dynamics of such a tie-up, people aware of the matter said.SAD under Sukhbir's father and ex-Punjab CM Parkash Singh Badal was the unquestioned big brother in the alliance, but the BJP wants a reset, citing growth in its vote share and decline in its former ally's since they parted ways. In the 2024 LS polls, the BJP had received over 18% of the vote and the SAD less than 15%.
Article Summary: Badal is believed to have raised the issue of "crumbling" law and order and "rampant" corruption in Punjab in his meeting with PM Modi. SAD leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with BJP, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since AAP came to office in 2022.

NEW DELHI: A former Calcutta high court judge who is presiding over one of the SIR appellate tribunals on Friday sought protection from the Supreme Court, claiming that before elections, she and her family members were repeatedly given life threats and their home CCTV connections were disconnected by miscreants.The petitioner, who is the advocate son of former judge Anindita Roy Saraswati, complained that the first threat letter was delivered at her residence on May 30, another on May 2, followed by cutting of the wires of CCTV cameras at their Kolkata residence.The petitioner said despite complaints to the Bidhannagar police commissionerate seeking a threat assessment, police protection, and forensic examination of the threat letters, no effective protection was provided to the former judge or her family members.The petition sought transfer of the investigations to the SC-monitored SIT.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was a serious matter and requested the Calcutta high court chief justice to look into the complaint for appropriate action.

Article Title: Government in Supreme Court: Audio clips linking Biren to Manipur unrest doctored
Article Text:
The apex court ordered that a copy of NFSU’s six-page report on the audio clips be supplied to both the petitioner and the Centre’s counsel

NEW DELHI: The Centre told the Supreme Court on Friday that audio recordings allegedly linking former Manipur CM N Biren Singh to the ethnic violence in the state were manipulated.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva that the forensic lab’s findings indicated that the recordings contained multiple alterations.“I want to urge that this writ petition be dismissed with costs. I spoke to the CFSL doctor, and I told them to send me a letter, and they have sent me a letter. This is clearly manipulated,” she said.The bench directed that the latest forensic report prepared by National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) be shared with Kuki Organisation for Human Rights, which is seeking investigation into audio clips allegedly implicating Biren Singh in the state’s ethnic violence.Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioner, said the report prepared by a forensic laboratory ‘Truth Labs’ had concluded with over 93% certainty that the voice in the recording was of Singh.The apex court ordered that a copy of NFSU’s six-page report on the audio clips be supplied to both the petitioner and the Centre’s counsel.
Article Summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court on Friday that audio recordings allegedly linking former Manipur CM N Biren Singh to the ethnic violence in the state were manipulated. The bench directed that the latest forensic report prepared by National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) be shared with Kuki Organisation for Human Rights, which is seeking investigation into audio clips.

Article Title: Iltija faces FIR, questioning over 'assault' on cop, accuses police of manhandling; Omar calls it 'fixed match'
Article Text:
Police have alleged that she bit the forearm of an officer during the protest, causing an injury

SRINAGAR: With J&K Police and Iltija Mufti locked up in a battle over allegations of assault and manhandling, chief minister Omar Abdullah Friday accused them of playing a “fixed match” in a bid to restore PDP’s credibility.Iltija, who accused police of manhandling her during the Aug 4-5 protest in Kashmir on the anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 , was Friday called to Kothibagh police station in Srinagar and questioned for nearly two hours over her alleged assault on a cop. Police have alleged that she bit the forearm of an officer during the protest, causing an injury.When asked about PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti’s criticism of the action against her daughter, Omar told reporters: “Please don’t ask me to comment on this fixed match. Whenever PDP’s political image weakens, agencies step in to help restore its credibility as they are the party’s mai baap. This party didn’t rise on its own, and it was made by agencies (a euphemism widely used by NC to refer to intelligence agencies).”Questioning the claims and counter-claims, Omar said: “Is Iltija Mufti a five-year-old child that she would bite someone? This entire episode is a fixed match and an unnecessary attempt to distract people from the real issues.”While police did not issue any statement on Iltija’s questioning, she said she was willing to cooperate with any investigation. However, she added: “I am neither the first nor the last Kashmiri to be summoned. My fight is not personal. I am here to fight for every Kashmiri.”On the CM’s remark, Iltija said: “Omar Sahib keeps giving the BJP a clean chit. He no longer speaks about Article 370 or special status. During the elections, he spoke about it every day. Now, it has become easier for him to target PDP than to question BJP.”Iltija has been booked under BNS sections 121, 132 and 191 for assault on public servants and rioting. Police alleged that during the protest on Aug 4, Iltija grabbed an officer on duty and bit his forearm, causing an injury and bleeding.Iltija, on the other hand, claimed she was manhandled by a woman IPS officer of SP rank, along with other police personnel and her own PSO, and added that she intended to take the matter to court.
Article Summary: J&K Police and Iltija Mufti locked up in a battle over allegations of assault and manhandling. Chief minister Omar Abdullah Friday accused them of playing a ‘fixed match’ in a bid to restore PDP’s credibility.Iltija has been booked under BNS sections 121, 132 and 191 for assault on public servants.

NEW DELHI: India has formally identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official map of the country, a move that comes amid China's repeated attempts to rename places in the border state.The government said the exercise is intended to ensure the correct identification of these places and improve public awareness of their geographical and historical significance."Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map of Arunachal Pradesh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," an official statement said.New Delhi has consistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, describing the exercise as "vain and preposterous". India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country.Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and their role in past India-China military confrontations.Among them is Long Ju, one of the earliest flashpoints between the two countries.Chinese troops entered the area in 1959, years before the 1962 war.The official map also includes Maja village in Upper Subansiri district near Long Ju, Bisa village and the strategically significant mountain passes of Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.Another key location is Thag La, the high-altitude pass where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place.Jairampur in Changlang district has also been formally identified. The town serves as an important logistics hub for the movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar border.Other locations added to the map include the high-altitude lake Sambho Sarovar, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar, Jaswant Garh, Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar, Baisakhi, Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.Jaswant Garh commemorates Indian Army soldier Jaswant Singh Rawat , while the Sher-e-Thapa Memorial honours 1962 war hero Trilok Singh Thapa.India has repeatedly dismissed China's attempts to assign what it calls "fictitious names" to places in Arunachal Pradesh, saying such efforts seek to create "baseless narratives" and cannot alter the "undeniable" reality on the ground. New Delhi has also warned that such actions could undermine efforts to improve bilateral ties.China first issued a list of six standardised names for places in what it calls Zangnan in 2017. It followed this with a second list covering 15 locations in 2021 and another naming 11 places in 2023. Beijing uses the name Zangnan to refer to Arunachal Pradesh, a claim India has consistently rejected.

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday appealed to people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles until the government makes its stand clear on E20 fuel.Kejriwal alleged that the government had not conducted proper testing for E20 fuel and claimed that its implementation had led to a significant drop in the mileage of vehicles.He said the mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs and other four-wheelers had dropped by around 25-30 per cent.Addressing a press conference in Goa, Kejriwal said, "Till such a time, the government makes its intention clear, I appeal to the people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles. The government did not conduct any testing for E20 fuel."Kejriwal said people in Goa were particularly affected by the decision, claiming that around 45 per cent of families in the state own a car and around 86 per cent of people own a two-wheeler.He said around 85-90 per cent of families in Goa could be affected by the decision due to the high ownership of vehicles in the state."The Modi government has aggressively implemented E20 across the country. People across the country are very unhappy about it. The mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs, and four-wheelers has dropped significantly. There has been an almost 25-30 per cent drop in mileage...Peoplein Goa are disproportionately affected by this decision. Nationally, only around 7% of households own a car, but in Goa, almost 45 per cent of families own a car. Around 86 per cent of people in Goa own a two-wheeler. Obviously, there is some overlap, many households own both a four-wheeler and a two-wheeler. So, we can understand that around 85-90 per cent of families in Goa are affected by this decision," Kejriwal said.Kejriwal said countries that adopted E20 fuel took several years to fully implement the policy, citing Brazil as an example.He said Brazil introduced E5 in 1931 and E20 in 1985, taking around 50-55 years to move from E5 to E20. He added that Brazil had only recently moved towards E100, using pure ethanol with flex-fuel vehicles that can run without petrol.He added, "Around the world, countries that implemented E20 gave themselves 10, 15, or even 20 years before fully implementing the policy. Brazil is at the forefront. Brazil now uses E100, meaning pure ethanol is also used, with flex-fuel vehicles that can run without petrol. But Brazil took 50 years to move to E20. In 1931, Brazil introduced E5, and in 1985, it introduced E20. It took them 50-55 years to reach E20. And only now have they moved to E100. " (ANI)
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday appealed to people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles until the government makes its stand clear on E20 fuel. He said the mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars and SUVs had dropped by around 25-30 per cent.

NEW DELHI: What began as a routine police recruitment result in Chhattisgarh quickly turned into an internet sensation after candidates with names such as 'News', 'Space Rani', 'He Ram', 'Bhakt Prahlad' and 'Tufail' appeared on the list of successful applicants, sparking disbelief, political allegations and eventually, a defence from the candidates themselves.The unusual names, which surfaced in the results of the Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission's (CGPSC) preliminary examination for police recruitment, prompted the opposition Congress to question the credibility of the selection process.The commission, however, dismissed the allegations, insisting that the names were genuine and matched the details submitted by candidates during registration.The controversy erupted after the results of the preliminary examination for 341 posts of subedar, sub-inspector and platoon commander were declared on August 4. A total of 7,301 candidates qualified for the mains examination.According to the CGPSC, the candidates had appeared for document verification, physical tests and the preliminary examination under the same names, which were also printed on their admit cards.Former chief minister Bhupesh Baghel mocked the list after sharing it on X."The Public Relations Department should spend Rs 1 crore daily on advertisements to display this achievement at public intersections so that, in the coming days, 'Radio' and 'Space Raja' might also succeed in some examination."State Congress communication wing chief Sushil Anand Shukla accused the BJP government of failing to deliver transparent recruitment despite promising PSC examinations on the lines of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).He alleged that the names reflected the alleged "negligence" of the CGPSC and the state government and claimed that several recruitment and promotion examinations held over the past two-and-a-half years had come under suspicion.Rejecting the allegations, the CGPSC described the claims circulating on social media as "misleading and baseless" and said they unfairly ridiculed candidates over their names."The names of the candidates displayed in the examination result are the same as those entered by them in their online application forms, which they finally submitted. The candidates appeared for document and physical tests as well as the preliminary examination under these names, and their names were also displayed accordingly on their admit cards," it stated.The commission urged candidates and the public not to believe misinformation and rely only on information published on its official website.As the debate gathered pace online, several candidates clarified that the names attracting attention were the same as those recorded in their official documents."My name is News Kumar Pradhan. My surname was not added to my Class 10 marksheet. My marksheets of Classes 10 and 12 and Aadhaar card carry the name News, without the surname. People think that the name is incorrect," said News Kumar Pradhan, who qualified in the preliminary examination. He added that he is from Bhatanpali village in Raigarh district.Tufail, a 29-year-old candidate from Nayapara in Raipur district, said his name appeared the same in all official records."After the result was released, rumours are being spread about names such as Spacerani, News and Tufail without any information or facts. These are the names of students who have prepared for the examination for years," he said.He appealed against spreading rumours and said such claims were hurting the morale of candidates from ordinary families.Another successful candidate, He Ram, said there was nothing unusual about the way his name was recorded."My name is He Ram, and I have qualified the PSC preliminary examination. Some people are raising objections over my name. My surname is Kashyap, but it is not mentioned in any of my documents. Hence, I entered only my name while filling the form," he told PTI.Bhakt Prahlad also clarified that his name was correctly recorded in all official documents."My surname is not mentioned. Please do not spread confusion regarding my name," he said.
Article Summary: Candidates with names such as 'News', 'Space Rani', 'He Ram', 'Bhakt Prahlad' and 'Tufail' appeared on the list of successful applicants. The unusual names prompted the opposition Congress to question the credibility of the selection process. The commission dismissed the allegations, insisting that the names were genuine and matched the details submitted by candidates during registration.

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.
Article Summary: Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken- Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.

Article Title: Iran officials 'would not be surprised' if Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dies soon: Report
Article Text:
Mojtaba Khamenei in 'extremely critical condition', may die soon, Iranian sources say​

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ’s health has come under renewed scrutiny after IranWire, citing two sources close to President Masoud Pezeshkian’s administration, reported that senior officials are increasingly concerned about his condition.According to IranWire, Khamenei has not met any cabinet members since the February 28 US-Israeli strikes that killed his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with other members of his family. The outlet said rumours that the younger Khamenei is in an “extremely critical condition” and could die soon are circulating within Iran’s highest levels of government.One source close to the Pezeshkian administration told IranWire that Khamenei’s physical condition was poor, adding that officials “would not be surprised” if they soon heard news of his death.The claims have not been independently verified. Iranian authorities have not announced that Khamenei is critically ill, while reports circulating in Israeli media have also claimed that he was recently taken to hospital. These reports cite Iranian sources but have not provided independent evidence of his current condition.Also read: Iran President met a 'voice in the dark', isn't sure it was Mojtaba Khamenei: Report The speculation has been amplified by Khamenei’s unusually low public profile since taking over as supreme leader.He has made no public appearances or televised speeches since assuming the position, with Iranian state media publishing only written statements attributed to him.That absence has led to repeated questions about his health and ability to govern, particularly after reports that he was injured in the February strike that killed his father.Iranian officials have previously disputed reports that his injuries were severe. State-linked officials have described his injuries as limited and maintained that he remains involved in strategic decision-making.President Pezeshkian himself said in a state television interview this week that communicating with Khamenei was currently “very difficult”, adding another layer to speculation surrounding the supreme leader's condition.Separately, a report by Iran International, said Pezeshkian was taken to an undisclosed location in Tehran for a brief meeting with a man presented as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. According to the report, the meeting took place inside a darkened vehicle and Pezeshkian was unable to see the man’s face. He later reportedly questioned whether the voice he heard actually belonged to Khamenei.The claims come as Iran remains under intense pressure following the conflict with the US and Israel and amid difficult negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz. The Wall Street Journal reported that Pezeshkian and other officials have struggled to gain access to Khamenei, who has remained largely absent from public view.
Article Summary: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's health has come under renewed scrutiny. Sources close to President Masoud Pezeshkian's administration say senior officials are increasingly concerned about his condition. Khamenei has not met any cabinet members since the February 28 US-Israeli strikes that killed his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Article Title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts
