Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey Friday signed a trilateral defence agreement aimed at strengthening their collective security as the conflict involving Iran continues to fuel instability across the West Asia.The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in the city.According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation".The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression and stipulates that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all, they said in a joint statement.The Pakistani ministry said the agreement reflects "the three states’ shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future."Also read: Evening news wrap: CBI chargesheet alleges NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG, MEA rejects US criticism of of FCRA Bill & more It added that "The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all."Meanwhile, India reacted to the development, saying "developments were closely watched".Responding to reports on the agreement, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “The pact between the three countries is, again, a development that we are closely following, and we will keep you updated on that.”The deal comes as Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries continue to face missile attacks and disruptions to energy shipments amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its regional allies. The war escalated after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28, triggering a wider regional crisis.A Turkish official said the agreement was purely defensive, was not aimed at any particular country and remained open to participation by other regional nations. The official also said it would not replace any existing bilateral or multilateral security arrangements.Analysts said the summit carried significant geopolitical weight at a time of growing uncertainty in the region."The political symbolism of the summit is significant. Three of the Muslim world's most influential states are convening at a moment of heightened uncertainty, demonstrating a growing willingness among regional and middle powers to coordinate more closely on security matters," Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi-based Gulf Research Center, told new agency Reuters."If institutionalised and translated into concrete cooperation, the trilateral framework could strengthen the three countries' collective diplomatic and defense weight while contributing to the emergence of a more regionally driven security architecture," Sager added.Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan each bring distinct strategic strengths to the partnership. Turkey has Nato's second-largest military, Saudi Arabia is one of the world's biggest oil exporters and custodian of Islam's holiest sites, while Pakistan is the only Muslim-majority country with nuclear weapons.The agreement follows months of discussions on expanding regional security cooperation. Earlier this year, Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan had said Ankara supported a broader regional security platform to promote stability.Experts believe the pact builds on long-standing military ties among the three countries. Pakistan has trained Saudi security forces for decades, while Turkey and Pakistan have cooperated on defence equipment and military training. Saudi Arabia also signed a major deal in 2023 to purchase Turkish drones.Mansoor Ahmed of the Australian National University's Strategic and Defence Studies Centre said Pakistan and Turkey could contribute advanced defence manufacturing capabilities, while Saudi Arabia could provide financial and technological investment.He added, however, that the new agreement was unlikely to include a nuclear component because Pakistan's nuclear deterrent remains focused on India.Pakistan has also expanded its military presence in Saudi Arabia in recent months by deploying thousands of troops, fighter aircraft, drones and air defence systems. It has simultaneously pursued broader security partnerships with Gulf countries, including talks with Kuwait on an expanded defence arrangement linked to energy cooperation and investment.
Article Summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed a trilateral defence agreement. The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression. An armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all. The deal comes as Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries continue to face missile attacks.

Article Title: NEET paper leak: CBI claims NTA experts breached 'secrecy pact', face life term, Rs 1 cr fine
Article Text:
Criminal breach of trust by a public servant under Section 316(5) of the BNS carries the maximum punishment of life imprisonment.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Three National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case breached their "obligation of secrecy" and circulated confidential question papers despite signing confidentiality undertakings, the CBI has alleged in its charge sheet filed before a Delhi court, news agency PTI reported.According to the charge sheet, the accused — biology subject expert Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, chemistry subject expert P V Kulkarni, and physics subject expert Manisha Sanjay Havaldar — have been booked under provisions that could attract life imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 crore.PTI reported that the CBI has treated the three as "public servants" while invoking provisions of the Prevention of Corruption (PC) Act, saying they had been entrusted with confidential property, namely the NEET-UG question papers, by the NTA in their capacity as subject experts.The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, is conducted by the NTA for admissions to undergraduate medical courses. The agency cancelled the examination held on May 3 after allegations of a paper leak and conducted a re-examination on June 21. Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan later resigned following nationwide protests over the controversy.Also read: NEET UG 2027 computer-based exam not final yet, Centre tells Supreme Court According to the charge sheet, all three experts had signed a "certificate of confidentiality", declaring that they were "not directly or indirectly involved in coaching for any entrance examination conducted by NTA, that the question/question paper would not be written or typed personally by them, that it would be kept under lock and key while in their possession, and that they would not retain any note, copy or rough draft of questions".However, the CBI alleged that the trio violated these commitments.The agency's final report stated that Mandhare conducted coaching classes from her residence in Pune, Kulkarni held "special classes" for candidates shortly before the examination at his residence and elsewhere in Pune, while Havaldar allegedly circulated confidential question papers herself and through her associates."Thus, the investigation establishes that, despite being entrusted with confidential work as a Biology subject expert for NEET UG 2026, accused Manisha Gurunath Mandhare was involved in coaching candidates, was connected with the circulation of confidential questions prior to the examination, received and handled such material through electronic means and through coaccused persons, facilitated the printing and onward handing over of question notes for unlawful gain," the charge sheet said.The report further alleged that despite being entrusted with confidential work as a chemistry subject expert, Kulkarni "conducted special classes immediately before the examination, shared leaked Chemistry questions with candidates for monetary gain, remained in contact with candidates, parents and co-accused persons, participated in the collection and receipt of money, and was part of the wider conspiracy for leaking confidential examination material before the exam".According to the CBI, Havaldar, despite being bound by a confidentiality undertaking, was involved in leaking and circulating physics questions before the examination, either directly or through associates.The charge sheet alleged that Havaldar transmitted and handled confidential material electronically, facilitated the printing and delivery of leaked question notes, remained in contact with co-accused persons and acted for monetary gain.PTI reported that the CBI has invoked provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act relating to criminal misconduct by a public servant. Under the Act, a public servant commits criminal misconduct if they dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriate property entrusted to them or permit another person to do so. The agency argued that since the trio had been entrusted with confidential question papers by the NTA, they were deemed public servants for the purpose of the law.Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, the accused face imprisonment of up to 10 years along with a fine.The charge sheet also invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including criminal conspiracy, causing disappearance of evidence, criminal breach of trust by a public servant, receiving stolen property and cheating.Among these offences, criminal breach of trust by a public servant under Section 316(5) of the BNS carries the maximum punishment of life imprisonment.In addition, the three have been booked under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, including provisions relating to "organised paper leak", which prescribe imprisonment of not less than five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of not less than Rs 1 crore, according to the charge sheet.
Article Summary: Three subject experts accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case breached their "obligation of secrecy" and circulated confidential question papers. The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate) is conducted by the NTA for admissions to undergraduate medical courses. The agency cancelled the examination held on May 3 after allegations of a paper leak and conducted a re- examination on June 21.

Article Title: CJP announces leadership line-up: Abhijeet Dipke takes charge as convener, check who gets what post
Article Text:
The announcement followed a two-day meeting of the CJP core team, where the party also named chief spokesperson Saurav Das and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka as co-conveners

Who Gets What: CJP's National Working Committee Line-Up

CJP's Expansion Roadmap





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its organisational framework, with founder Abhijeet Dipke appointed as the National Convener.The announcement followed a two-day meeting of the CJP core team, where the party also named chief spokesperson Saurav Das and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka as Co-Conveners, along with assigning responsibilities to other key members.The newly formed committee will oversee the party’s expansion strategy, including the formation of state coordination committees, Lok Sabha-level units, and city-level teams across the country in the next six months, the CJP said.Abhijeet Dipke (30) — Founder & National ConvenerSaurav Das (27) — Co-ConvenerAshutosh Ranka (30) — Co-ConvenerAjinkya Shinde (35) — National Organisation In-ChargeDeepak Baliyan (26) — Organisation Co-In-Charge & North Zone LeadAafreen Nawaz (34) — National SecretaryRatna Singh (31) — Legal Affairs LeadVaishnavi Gaur (29) — Research & Policy LeadRohan Deshpande (31) — Technology LeadVijay Reddi Mallangi (30) — Media LeadYogesh Ingale (33) — Finance & West Zone LeadAnkit Bhardwaj (35) — East & North East Zone LeadCJP said it will launch a membership drive through its website, inviting students, young professionals and workers to join the organisation.The outfit clarified that it is not collecting any funds as part of the membership campaign.The organisation also reiterated that it has no immediate plans to enter electoral politics. "Adding one more political party will not be useful at this time. We will work at the grassroots level," CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said."We are launching a membership drive through our website. Students, young professionals and workers can join us to raise their voices unitedly, " Saurav Das told PTI.Meanwhile, CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka said a delegation will visit student protesters in Jharkhand, where an agitation over alleged recruitment exam irregularities has entered its 13th day. Six demonstrators are currently on hunger strike.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its organisational framework. The newly formed committee will oversee the party’s expansion strategy, including the formation of state coordination committees, Lok Sabha-level units, and city-level teams across the country in the next six months.

Article Title: 'Waves without quake': Mystery well in Gujarat baffles locals as water ripples for 5 days; watch
Article Text:
Villagers, commuters and passersby gathered in large numbers at the spot to witness the unusual activity, which has been occurring for the past five days.

(With agency inputs)





MORBI: An 18-foot-deep well in a remote village in Gujarat’s Morbi district has drawn widespread attention after it began showing continuous waves and ripples on its water surface, leaving locals intrigued.While the unusual movement has sparked curiosity, officials said no seismic activity has been detected in the area to explain the phenomenon. They suggested that air escaping through cracks or gaps in the rocks beneath the well could be causing the water to ripple.Villagers, commuters and passersby gathered in large numbers at the spot to witness the unusual activity, which has been occurring for the past five days.The mysterious waves have left locals puzzled, with some fearing a possible connection to seismic activity.However, district Geologist J S Vadher ruled out such a possibility, saying the phenomenon was unlikely to be linked to any seismic activity."This is not a seismic activity. Prima facie, it appears that following heavy upstream rainfall, groundwater is recharging and air trapped in the pore spaces of rocks is being released, causing the disturbance in the well," Vadher told PTI on Thursday.He further said that officials had consulted the Institute of Seismological Research in Gandhinagar, which confirmed that no active fault line exists in the area.Morbi district collector Swapnil Khare said a team from Gandhinagar will investigate the unusual phenomenon to determine its cause."We have informed the Gujarat government about it, and a team from Gandhinagar will visit the site for further investigation," he said.The owner of the farm where the well is located, Pranjivan Sadariya, said he first noticed the unusual activity on August 2."When I arrived at my farm on Sunday, water from the well was spilling over the edge, and the same thing has continued ever since," he said.Sadariya added that the well was constructed about three months ago.
Article Summary: An 18-foot-deep well in a remote village in Gujarat’s Morbi district has drawn widespread attention after it began showing continuous waves and ripples on its water surface. Villagers, commuters and passersby gathered in large numbers at the spot to witness the unusual activity, which has been occurring for the past five days.

Article Title: 'Exercise restraint, act according to law': US urges Pakistan amid PoK crackdown
Article Text:
Representative image

United States on Friday urged the Pakistan government to exercise restraint amid its ongoing crackdown on citizens following violent protests.Speaking to news agency ANI, a US state department spokesperson urged Pakistani authorities to create conditions for free and fair elections that can be conducted peacefully."As with electoral proceedings around the world, we urge officials to create the conditions for free and fair elections that can be conducted in a peaceful manner, including ensuring access to information," the spokesperson said.The state department also called on local authorities to exercise restraint and act in accordance with the country's laws and Constitution."We call on all protesters to express their grievances peacefully, and we call on local authorities to exercise restraint, act in accordance with their country's laws and Constitution, and respect fundamental freedoms as they seek to maintain order," the spokesperson added.The remarks came as at least 30 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July.The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June over the contentious 12 refugee seats. It has alleged that Pakistan's establishment manipulates these seats to install a prime minister of its choice to lead the so-called PoK government.According to JAAC, more than 40 people were killed during the first phase of polling on July 27. It also claims that around 400 protesters have been killed since the first week of June.The Shehbaz Sharif government has rejected the claims, calling the figures "overly exaggerated"."The number of people killed in the protests is in two digits. Moreover, security personnel have also lost their lives," Prime Minister's Adviser Rana Sanaullah said in a recent television interview.Meanwhile, voting in seven of the 11 constituencies scheduled for the third phase of polls in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir on August 10 has been postponed indefinitely due to "concerns over the law-and-order situation", authorities announced on Friday.After the first and second phases of polling, which were marred by violent protests, were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively, voting was scheduled for Monday in 11 constituencies of the Poonch Division in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.There are 53 seats in the so-called PoK Legislative Assembly - 45 are directly elected, while eight are reserved for women, technocrats and clerics.The second phase of polling on August 2 was marred by violence and allegations of rigging. One person was killed and several others were injured. The phase also included voting for the 12 refugee seats, which are at the centre of the ongoing controversy.Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) swept the second phase, winning 16 seats, while Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) secured the remaining five.In the first phase on July 27, PML-N won nine of the 13 seats, while PPP won four. With the first two phases combined, PML-N has already secured 24 seats.
Article Summary: U.S. urges Pakistan to create conditions for free and fair elections that can be conducted peacefully. At least 30 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July. Banned Joint Awami Action Committee has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir since June over the contentious 12 refugee seats.

Article Title: Watch: Accident victim's fractured leg tied with carton at Bihar Hospital; probe ordered
Article Text:
Kunal was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg.





PATNA: A road accident victim at Manjhaul Sub-Divisional Hospital in Bihar's Begusarai district was allegedly treated by immobilising his fractured leg with pieces of a medicine carton instead of a plaster, triggering outrage after a video of the procedure went viral on social media.The patient, identified as Kunal Kumar, is a resident of Maheshwara village under the Nawkothi police station limits. The incident took place on the evening of August 3.According to his family members, Kunal was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg and was taken to Manjhaul Sub-Divisional Hospital by locals and relatives.At the hospital, staff on duty allegedly placed two pieces of a medicine carton on either side of his fractured leg and secured them tightly with rope and bandages. After administering first aid, doctors referred him to Sadar Hospital in Begusarai.In the viral video, Kunal can be seen lying on a hospital bed with a pharmaceutical carton tied around his injured leg.When contacted, Manjhaul Hospital in-charge Dr Abhinav Priyadarshi defended the procedure. He admitted to the shortcomings but said the treatment was in line with medical protocol."What you are calling a 'koot' or carton is called a splint in medical science.When a bone is broken, it is necessary to immobilise that part to prevent further internal damage," Dr Priyadarshi said.He said there was no orthopaedic doctor or dresser available at the time, and the hospital also lacked plaster facilities."To relieve the patient's pain and prevent the leg from moving while shifting him to a higher centre, using available material as a splint is justified under medical protocol," he added.Begusarai civil surgeon Dr Ashok Kumar said he had taken note of the viral video."I have received information about the incident. The video has gone viral. I will get it investigated, and if anyone is found guilty, action will be taken," he said.Dr Kumar added that using a carton as a temporary splint is recognised in medical practice for emergency first aid. "But if this was done at the hospital, it will be investigated," he said.When asked, Manjhaul Hospital In-charge Dr Abhinav Priyadarshi defended the procedure. He admitted to the shortcomings but said it was done as per medical protocol.“What you are calling ‘koot’ or carton is called a splint in medical science. When a bone is broken, it is necessary to immobilize that part to prevent further internal damage,” Dr Priyadarshi said.He said there was no orthopaedic doctor or dresser available at the time and there was no arrangement for plaster either.“To give the patient relief from pain and to prevent the leg from moving while shifting him to a higher centre, tying a splint with available material is justified under medical protocol,” he added.
Article Summary: Kunal Kumar was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg and was taken to Manjhaul Sub- Divisional Hospital. Staff allegedly placed two pieces of a medicine carton on either side of his fractured leg and secured them tightly with rope and bandages.

Article Title: 'We demand that NTA be dissolved': CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on CBI chargesheet in NEET 2026 case
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has demanded that the National Testing Agency (NTA) be dissolved and converted into a national technical testing commission following the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.“I just came to know that CBI has filed a chargesheet in the NEET 2026 case which involves a lot of NTA officers,” Ranka said.He also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEET-UG 2025 cases, and called for those responsible to be brought to justice.Ranka said the government should address what he described as structural problems affecting the country's examination system, including examination infrastructure and vendors involved in conducting exams.“It is imperative that the government takes steps to solve these structural issues that are plaguing the systems of this country, not just NTA but the entire exam system,” he said.“The exam infrastructure which includes the vendors have to be audited properly and it has to be made sure that the country doesn't see any more paper leaks,” he added.What does the CBI chargesheet allege?The CBI has alleged that the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak was part of a coordinated, multi-state conspiracy in which NTA-appointed subject experts allegedly accessed confidential examination papers and passed them on to middlemen and coaching operators for money.In a chargesheet filed before the special CBI court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue, the agency named 13 accused, including three NTA-appointed subject experts: Botany specialist Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, Chemistry expert Prahlad Vithalrao Kulkarni and Physics expert Manisha Sanjay Havaldar.According to the CBI, the leaked questions were circulated through a network of intermediaries before allegedly reaching candidates who paid for access to them.The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The agency alleged that forensic examination of seized mobile phones, pen drives and other electronic devices recovered PDF and image files containing NEET-UG 2026 questions.Investigators said the files were exchanged through Telegram, WhatsApp and other messaging platforms several days before the examination.The chargesheet names Tejas Shah, Shivraj Motegaonkar, Dr Manoj Shirure, Manisha Sanjay Waghmare, Dhananjay Lokhande, Shubham Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal in addition to the three NTA experts.The CBI has alleged that the accused played different roles in sourcing, circulating and distributing the leaked questions and handling financial transactions.The agency's investigation also included statements from candidates and their family members.In one instance, the CBI alleged that a candidate and her father were offered access to the NEET-UG 2026 question paper for Rs 4 lakh, along with coaching support and offline revision classes conducted by one of the NTA subject experts.The CBI said forensic evidence, chat records, recovered documents and witness statements support its allegations of criminal conspiracy, abuse of official position by public servants and illegal circulation of confidential examination material before the NEET-UG 2026 examination.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts. Ranka also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEet-UG 2025 cases.

Article Title: Nolan Wells update: Ben Crump’s one-word response follows major legal move by Mississippi teen’s friends
Article Text:
Nolan Wells update: Ben Crump’s one-word response follows major legal move by Mississippi teen’s friends

Ben Crump dismisses Edward Andrew Paltzik’s appointment in Nolan Wells case

The New York Times

Warren Hudson’s family, Brandon Tatum respond as fundraiser crosses $161,000

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The legal battle surrounding the death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells has taken another turn after three of his friends hired attorney Edward Andrew Paltzik, a lawyer known for representing President Donald Trump in several high-profile lawsuits. When asked about Paltzik joining the defense team, Ben Crump, who represents Wells’ family, gave a one-word response. Speaking to TMZ, Crump called it a “distraction.” His comment came as investigators continue looking into Wells’ death and both sides push back against growing claims and speculation surrounding the case.According to TMZ, attorneys J. Tyler Cox and Edward Andrew Paltzik are now representing Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour, the three friends who were with Nolan Wells before he was found dead following a boat trip last month.Paltzik is widely known for handling major defamation and media-related cases, including lawsuits involving President Donald Trump against CBS/Paramount,, and the BBC. His addition to the legal team comes as the three young men continue facing online accusations despite no official finding linking them to a crime.When TMZ asked Ben Crump what Paltzik’s involvement meant for the case, the civil rights attorney did not expand on his thoughts.Instead, he simply replied, “distraction.”Meanwhile, authorities are still investigating the events leading up to Wells’ death. At the same time, false claims, AI-generated videos, and misleading social media posts have continued to spread online. Those posts have fueled speculation even though investigators have not announced any conclusions about what happened.Reports also say the families of Wells’ friends have received threats since the teenager disappeared and was later found dead. The defense team has argued that online rumors have unfairly damaged the reputations of the young men before the investigation has been completed.The legal fight has now grown beyond the official investigation. Warren Hudson’s father, Benjamin Hudson, launched a GiveSendGo fundraiser to help cover legal costs for the teenagers.In the fundraiser description, Benjamin Hudson said he plans to sue Ben Crump over what he believes were false statements about his son and the other boys. The page states, “Since Nolan’s death, Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, Morgan Seymour, and many others have been inundated with death threats, threats of violence, and defamation. They have been falsely and wrongly blamed by individuals online and in the media of either directly or indirectly having a hand in Nolan’s death. ”As of the latest update, the fundraiser has collected more than $161,000 toward its $200,000 goal.Conservative commentator Brandon Tatum also reacted after Paltzik joined the legal team. Tatum had previously invited Warren Hudson onto his podcast to share his side of the story. He also interviewed Tracestin (Trace) Shepherd, who described himself as Nolan Wells’ best friend. However, Wells’ family later said they had never heard of Shepherd.In a post on X, Tatum wrote that the teenagers “have been forced to fight for their reputations and futures,” adding that they should be allowed to grieve their friend. He also said, “These families are no longer leaving their names at the mercy of the online mob. They now have one of America’s most formidable defamation attorneys in their corner-and, in my opinion, the people responsible for pushing these allegations are about to learn why we have a court system. ”Separately, Bart Edmiston Jr., who was reportedly on a different boat near Horn Island on the day Wells disappeared, sent a cease-and-desist letter to OnlyFans model Kymbra Li after she allegedly linked him to Wells’ death. Authorities have not announced any final findings, and the investigation into Nolan Wells’ death remains active.
Article Summary: Edward Andrew Paltzik has been hired by Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour. The three friends were with 18-year-old Nolan Wells before he was found dead last month. Authorities are still investigating the events leading up to Wells’ death. Warren Hudson’s father, Benjamin Hudson, launched a GiveSendGo fundraiser to help cover legal costs.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina-linked exiled cricketer ready to return, face murder trial 'if security is guaranteed'
Article Text:
Shakib Al Hasan, Sheikh Hasina

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Shakib Al Hasan return to Bangladesh to face trial? Yes, he should return. No, he should stay abroad. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan is ready to return home after two years in exile, face trial in the cases against him, including a murder charge, and play a farewell series if the government guarantees his safety, news agency Reuters reported.Shakib, a former lawmaker from former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League, has been living in the United States since Hasina's government was removed in a student-led uprising in August 2024.The 39-year-old has not retired from international cricket and said he still hopes to play one final series for Bangladesh at home before representing the country at the 2027 ODI World Cup.Shakib's situation reflects the wider impact of Hasina's removal from power, with several of her political allies facing criminal cases and remaining outside Bangladesh. His return could also indicate whether the government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is willing to allow members of the former ruling party to return. Hasina herself has announced plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite being sentenced to death there."If I get the clearance from the government that my security will be ensured, I am happy to go back, face the court trial and everything that's needed to be done," Shakib told Reuters."I know I haven't done anything," he said, while giving his most detailed account of the past two years abroad.Hasina, who has been living in India, was sentenced to death in absentia over the crackdown on the Bangladesh protests, which the United Nations said killed about 1,400 people. She has told Reuters that she and other Awami League leaders plan to return to Bangladesh voluntarily in December.Shakib said he wanted to return immediately, but if that was not possible, he would try to return with Hasina."Whatever the captain says, we follow her," he said. "I think they will decide it better, and we will follow the instructions given to us."Shakib also defended his virtual appearance at the press conference in Delhi alongside Hasina on Wednesday. After the event, his unoccupied house in Bangladesh was attacked.He said he had only appealed for peace and the progress of Bangladesh and had no regrets about attending the event.Shakib also said that, through his lawyer, he had written to Bangladesh's interior, law and sports ministries under the previous interim government, as well as the police, asking for what he described as fabricated cases against him to be dropped, but did not receive any response.He added that he is willing to speak to Prime Minister Rahman about returning to Bangladesh.
Article Summary: Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan is ready to return home after two years in exile. He has been living in the United States since Hasina's government was removed in a student-led uprising in August 2024. Hasina herself has announced plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite being sentenced to death there.

Article Title: US appeals court halts Trump's $400 million ballroom project, grants 14 days for Supreme Court appeal
Article Text:
A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House (AP image)

A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House, dealing a significant setback to the president's plan to reshape the historic complex.In a 2-1 ruling, the Washington-based US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which challenged the project after the administration demolished the White House's East Wing and began building a 90,000-square-foot ballroom without congressional approval, cites Reuters.The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.The ruling comes after US District Judge Richard Leon had twice blocked above-ground construction while allowing underground work to continue. Leon ruled that "no federal statute comes close to giving the President" the authority to construct the ballroom without approval from Congress.The Trump administration has defended the project, saying the ballroom is needed to host large formal events while improving security at the White House.The ballroom is among several initiatives by Trump aimed at reshaping government buildings and national landmarks in Washington.During arguments before the appeals court in June, Justice Department lawyer Yaakov Roth argued that the judiciary had no role in reviewing the privately funded project."The courts have no role" in weighing the project, Roth said, adding that the preservation group's "architectural preference" against the ballroom should not outweigh national security concerns. He argued the former East Wing left "the president and others in the White House vulnerable to attack."Opposing the administration, Thaddeus Heuer, counsel for the National Trust for Historic Preservation, said the issue was not aesthetics but legal procedure. "They just don't want to go to Congress," Heuer told the court.Trump has repeatedly defended the ballroom and its rising cost, which has nearly doubled from initial estimates. In a post on Truth Social last month, he said the price increased because "it is approximately twice the size, and a far higher quality, than the original proposal," adding that "it will be magnificent, safe, and secure!"The ballroom case follows another recent legal setback for the administration after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been unlawfully added to the exterior of the Kennedy Center and ordered its removal.
Article Summary: A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House. In a 2-1 ruling, the court upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation. The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district, died in the blast. He worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: 2 Ghaziabad hospitals that turned away child rape victim to give parents Rs 12 lakh
Article Text:
Senior advocate N Hariharan said there are SC rulings mandating the hospitals to treat injured persons yet lapses continue to occur (AI Image)

Court flags gaps in law implementation





NEW DELHI: Seeking to escape criminal prosecution and compensation liability for turning away a minor girl grievously injured in a brutal sexual assault and who later died, two Ghaziabad hospitals on Friday undertook before Supreme Court to “donate” Rs 12 lakh to the child’s parents.Troubled by the insensitivity of the hospitals and Ghaziabad cops, a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it would consider laying down ‘must treat’ guidelines for hospitals and mandate police to video record complainants’ statements in sexual assault cases.Senior advocate N Hariharan, appearing for the victim’s parents, said Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita has provisions in this regard, but no one seems to follow it.Justice Bagchi said, “The law is there. SC rulings are there mandating medical institution to provide treatment. But these are ideals in rarefied atmosphere of court. What happens on ground... is far removed from ideals.”Police officers need to be sensitised, says CJISenior advocate N Hariharan said there are SC rulings mandating the hospitals to treat injured persons yet lapses continue to occur. Had any of the two hospitals given required treatment, the girl might have been alive today, he said.CJI said, "You are absolutely right. The child was treated with such insensitive, inhuman and deplorable manner, it aggravated her victimisation. We will lay down some guidelines in this regard. The police dealing with crime daily tend to become insensitive. Police officers are required to be periodically trained and sensitised to be extremely sympathetic to victims of crime. There was definitely some failure at crucial moments in this case both on the part of the police and the hospitals. "Justice Bagchi said, "The most important thing is preservation of life. That is where both the law enforcing agency as well as the medical institutions were found lacking."The bench sought suggestions from Hariharan and additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati for the court to issue some positive directions in this regard. "The statutory provisions are there but not implemented on ground level. How to fill that gap - we will issue certain directions," it said.Justice Bagchi referred to the golden period for treatment and said, "If immediate medical assistance was given to the child, she could have survived. The girl, who had suffered such a traumatic sexual assault, the barest thing the hospitals could have done is administer blood."
Article Summary: Two Ghaziabad hospitals on Friday undertook before Supreme Court to ‘donate’ Rs 12 lakh to the child’s parents. A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it would consider laying down ‘must treat’ guidelines for hospitals.

Article Title: New Delhi Woman Dies After Fall From Haiderpur Flyover, Police Probe
Article Text: New Delhi: A 42-year-old woman died after allegedly falling from a flyover near Haiderpur Metro Station Wednesday. Police are probing whether the incident was a case of suicide.The incident occurred while she was travelling on a motorcycle with her husband. According to police, the couple, along with their daughter, were returning from Kashmere Gate ISBT. They dropped their daughter at Mukarba Chowk, from where she went home, before the husband and wife continued towards their workplace.“During the journey, an argument reportedly broke out between the couple. Our preliminary inquiry suggests that the woman jumped from the flyover. We have a witness who saw the incident,” a police officer said. The investigation is underway to ascertain the exact sequence of events.
Article Summary: 42-year-old woman died after allegedly falling from a flyover near Haiderpur Metro Station. Police are probing whether the incident was a case of suicide. Incident occurred while she was travelling on a motorcycle with her husband. The couple, along with their daughter, were returning from Kashmere Gate ISBT.

Article Title: ‘Rude wake-up call’: Shashi Tharoor on CJP protests, says Gen Z will be largest voting bloc in 2029
Article Text:
Tharoor said young people are an increasingly significant segment of the population and will form the largest single voting bloc in the 2029 elections.

(With agency inputs)





MUMBAI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has said politicians must listen to young people and engage with them, arguing that Gen Z and Gen Alpha will play an increasingly important role in Indian politics and elections.Speaking about his interaction with young protesters, Tharoor said he went to Jantar Mantar during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests simply to listen to their concerns and did not deliver a speech.“I believe that in politics, you must listen to people and engage with them. Ultimately, politics is about the good of the country,” Tharoor said.He noted that young people would constitute a significant section of the electorate, adding that they would form the “largest single voting bloc” in the 2029 elections.“And young people are now an increasingly significant segment of our population. As I pointed out, they will be the largest single voting bloc in 2029. It is also in our political interest to listen to what they care about and what they want. So, I am very much inclined to talk to them,” Tharoor said."Even at Jantar Mantar, I went there only to listen. I did not give any speech at Jantar Mantar; I was simply listening to what they had to say.We have to listen. That is a very important message for all politicians, ” Tharoor told PTI.Shashi Tharoor said the ruling party had received a “rude wake-up call” following the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests, recent political developments and bypoll results.Speaking about the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s remarks, Tharoor said the CJP protests had demonstrated the growing influence of young voters and their concerns.He pointed to the CJP protests, the resignation of a minister and the passage of a bill, saying these developments showed the political impact of the movement.Tharoor also cited recent bypoll results, including Prashant Kishor’s victory in a BJP stronghold that the party had held for more than three decades. He also referred to the Congress retaining the Datia seat in Madhya Pradesh.“These are both Hindi heartland states,” Tharoor said, adding that the results indicated that the political landscape could be changing.Looking ahead to the upcoming electoral cycle, Tharoor said the Congress could have a strong opportunity in states going to polls next March.“I believe there is a good chance. We fortunately have in our system these different elections at different times. Already next March there'll be a few states coming into play where the Congress can be very much capable of winning those states,” he said.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says politicians must listen to young people and engage with them. He says Gen Z and Gen Alpha will play an increasingly important role in Indian politics and elections. He went to Jantar Mantar during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests simply to listen to their concerns and did not deliver a speech.

Article Title: Palghar man gets death for rape, murder of 9-year-old girl
Article Text:
The court took grave note of the brutality of the crime and the lack of remorse shown by the accused





Palghar: The District and Additional Sessions Court in Palghar on Friday sentenced a 46-year-old man to death for the rape and murder of a nine-year-old girl in a tribal hamlet of Dahanu on Sept 27, 2021. Judge A R Rahane also imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 on him.The victim, then aged nine years and eight months, had been sent by her mother to fetch supplies from a neighbourhood shop. According to the prosecution, the accused identified as Pramul, also known as Praful or Pramade Ratna Ghose, who lived nearby lured the child into his house, showed her obscene images on his mobile phone and sexually assaulted her.Following the assault, the girl began crying in pain. The accused offered her Rs 10 to buy snacks, but she insisted she would tell her family about the incident and attempted to run away. The accused allegedly grabbed a sickle from his house, chased the girl down and struck her repeatedly on the head, neck and face, inflicting around 15 fatal blows. A 40-year-old villager who tried to intervene was also attacked and seriously injured by the accused, who then allegedly attempted to destroy evidence at the scene.The court took grave note of the brutality of the crime and the lack of remorse shown by the accused, who reportedly displayed no contrition even after the sentence was pronounced.The case was investigated by then Assistant Superintendent of Police Nityanand Jha. Special Public Prosecutor Advocate Rekha Ivarale represented the state.Officials said this is perhaps the first instance in Palghar district where the death penalty has been imposed in a POCSO case involving such a brutal murder.
Article Summary: The court took grave note of the brutality of the crime and the lack of remorse shown by the accused. The victim, then aged nine years and eight months, had been sent by her mother to fetch supplies from a neighbourhood shop. A 40-year- old villager who tried to intervene was also attacked and seriously injured.
